class.name: NetwAuthFlow
class.brief_description: The base a game subclasses to decide which peers a session admits, returning for both ends of the handshake.

method.name: _credentials
method.description: The bytes this peer presents to the authority for the join it is attempting as [param username]. They reach the authority's [method _verify] unchanged, so their shape is this flow's own business.

method.name: _host_identity
method.description: The [NetwIdentity] a host claims for itself, which no peer verifies for it.

method.name: _prepare
method.description: Runs before [method _credentials] and gates it: bring-up waits on the returned [NetwPromise], which is where a flow fetches or refreshes whatever [method _credentials] is about to present for [param username]. Resolving with anything but [constant @GlobalScope.OK] abandons the join.

method.name: _verify
method.description: The authority's verdict on the [param data] peer [param peer_id] presented. Return [method AuthResult.accept] with the identity to seat it under, or [method AuthResult.reject] with the reason to hand back. [b]Server Only.[/b]

method.name: credentials
method.description: Returns [method _credentials], or [method credentials_default] when nothing overrode it.

method.name: credentials_default
method.description: Presents no bytes at all, which is what a flow that authenticates the host rather than the peer wants.

method.name: host_identity
method.description: Returns [method _host_identity], or [method host_identity_default] when nothing overrode it.

method.name: prepare
method.description: Returns [method _prepare], or [method prepare_default] when nothing overrode it.

method.name: prepare_default
method.description: Returns a [NetwPromise] already resolved with [constant @GlobalScope.OK], so bring-up never waits on a flow with nothing to fetch.

method.name: verify
method.description: Returns [method _verify], or [method verify_default] when nothing overrode it. [b]Server Only.[/b]

method.name: verify_default
method.description: Rejects, naming the missing override as the reason. An installed flow that never implements [method _verify] is a policy nobody wrote, and admitting on it would be the one failure mode authentication exists to prevent. [b]Server Only.[/b]
